full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original suit for Partition being Title Suit No. 37 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Gournadi against the defendant-opposite parties contending inter alia, that the suit jote appertaining to Mouza Horohoro under JL No. 176 corresponding to SA khatian No. 274 in plots No. 856/857 comprising an area of 82 decimals of land originally belonged to one Moti Lal and Sarda Sundari Debi in 04 annas and 12 annas share each. The land described in paragraph No. 1 of the plaint comprising an area of 201/2 decimals was correctly recorded in the name of Matilal Debnath, which was owned and possessed by Motilal and in the year 1958 he died leaving behind one daughter having son Laxmi Rani Debi. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Laxmi Rani as owner of the land mutated her name in a mutation proceeding and paid rent therein. Thereafter; on 23-9-1985 she gifted the suit land in favour of her three sons the plaintiffs No. 1-3. The plaintiff-petitioners after acquiring title in the suit land by virtue of that deed of gift from their mother, in the Mutation Case being No. 1376(1X-11) 85-86 mutated their names and possessing the same after payment of rent. The plaintiffs are possessing their portion of land in ejmali with other co-sharers of the holding and facing difficulty in ejmali possession and for that; they requested the defendants to make amicable partition in respect of their 201/2 decimals of land, but the defendants denied after claiming the suit property; on the basis of a forged sub-kabala deed executed by Matilal Debnath in favour of the defendant's predecessor, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for partition. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned senior Advocate Mr Debdas Samaddar appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that, the law is blind and nobody is above law. The learned Advocate further submits that it is decided by the learned court below that the title document of the plaintiff-petitioners is not a legal document by which the land can be transferred by Laxmi Rani in favour of her sons the plaintiffs. Furthermore; there is no evidence and pleading of the plaintiffs that Laxmi Rani had reversionary right from the admitted owner Motilal Debnath inasmuch as; she was the only daughter of Motilal having son at the time of death of Motilal Debnath. The title document of the plaintiffs i.e. the deed of gift as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs in their plaint has been decided a value less document under law having no legal force and realizing that fact; the plaintiff-petitioners rare now taking a new device to grab the property, bringing a new case without their pleadings and evidence on ,records that as reversioner they are entitled the suit land measuring 201/2 decimals of land in SA khatian No. 274 which stands recorded in the name of Motilal Debnath. The learned Advocate also submits that the judgment and decree of the learned lower appellate court is not perverse and the learned appellate court rightly after proper assessment of evidence, and appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit against the plaintiffs and in passing the impugned judgment and decree no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice has done by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned counsel argued that it is a decided matter that the' court cannot consider anything beyond the pleadings of the parties. The learned Advocate in support of his contention have referred some decisions of our Apex Court passed in the case of Shamsul Huda (Md) being dead his heirs Hafez Md Ismail vs Bangladesh, 5 BLC (AD) 108, on the provision laid down in Order VI, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case of Tara Mia vs Babru Mia, 12 BLC (AD) 222 on the provision laid down under Order VI, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and finally in the case of Md Hazrat Ali vs Joynal Abedin, 1986 BLD (AD) 45, on the inherent power of the Court. 

 12. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the plaintiff-petitioners instituted the original suit for partition for getting a separate saham in respect of the land described in schedule-'ka' of the plaint comprising an area of 201/2 decimals of land appertaining to J.L. No 176 under police station-Gournadi of. Bakerganj District in Mouza-176 Horohoro corresponding to plot No.856/857 under SA. khatian No. 274 comprising total area 82 decimals of land, out of which; claiming 04 annas share in the land of suit the holding the plaintiffs filed the original suit for partition along with a specific pleading that the suit land had been owning and possessing by the recorded tenant Motilal and in the year 1958 AD he died leaving behind his only daughter Laxmi Rani Debi who at the demise of her father Motilal inherited the suit land and thereafter transferred the suit land by a deed of gift dated 23-9-1985 in favour of her sons the present plaintiff-petitioners and thus the- plaintiffs have acquired title and interest in the suit land claimed by them.
